new.n: Miser's jar of gold under the woodshed, Traer (found 1904)
new.pl: His house lot in Traer; the woodshed stood at its NW corner. Lot not yet identified (Sanborn check pending).
new.st: A Traer capitalist who distrusted banks died in Dec 1904 leaving about $60,000. On his deathbed he told his banker of a glass jar of gold under the northwest corner of his woodshed, fed through a soldered gas pipe whose top lay a foot and a half underground. The banker probed with a pole, struck the pipe and recovered $2,500 or more in gold. His will left the farms to the Traer Methodist church and two Iowa charities.
src: Tama County will records vol. 4-5, will of 1 Sep 1899 (Ancestry)
pinev: 1900 census puts him in a house in Traer, not on his farms (Toledo was only the dateline); pin on Traer village, lot not identified.
new.tovw: Lead grade F (treasure thread): recovered by the banker in 1904; town lot look-only marker

tw-mi-agards-landing-gold.st: The 1938 feature: John Agard, a French trader, set up 8-10 cabins on the Paw Paw River bank a quarter mile below a lake in 1827; the stone and split-log canoe-landing rocks were still visible; he died in the fall of 1835 and was buried at the post; the gold cache was never found.
